title: Gateable Terraform plan/apply pipeline with OPA/Conftest checks for Private VPC deployments
creator: Isabel Moreno
description:
Goal: Implement a robust CI/CD workflow for Redwood Private (VPC) Terraform modules that enforces policy-as-code (OPA/Conftest), provides safe gated plan/apply paths, and enables automated health/drift checks. This work will enable self-service onboarding for customers and reduce manual ops for upgrades and patching.

Scope:
- GitHub Actions (or equivalent) pipelines for PR-time lint/plan and protected branch apply.
- OPA/Conftest policy suite enforcement during PRs and before apply.
- Separate plan outputs per environment and workspace isolation for customer accounts.
- Remote backend guarantees: S3+DynamoDB locking (or cloud equivalent) with documented state migration.
- Canary apply strategy for module upgrades (small subset of customers first).
- Drift detection scheduled job + alerts into PagerDuty and Console.
- Integration tests (Terratest) for core modules and upgrade paths.

Acceptance criteria:
1) PR pipeline runs: terraform fmt, tflint, tfsec (optional), terraform init/plan with allow-dirty=false, OPA/Conftest policy run that fails PR on violations.
2) Protected branch: merge triggers gated apply that requires human approval for P0 changes and automatic apply for low-risk patches per policy.
3) All applies use remote state with locks; pipeline verifies lock and state consistency before apply.
4) Canary upgrade process documented and automatable (runbook + pipeline job).
5) Scheduled drift-check job runs nightly and creates incidents for divergence beyond threshold.
6) Demo of onboarding a new customer using modules + pipeline documented in Confluence.

Key trade-offs considered:
- Strict blocking policies reduce operational risk but slow velocity for internal teams; decided to allow policy exemptions via an approvals flow for emergency fixes.
- Run tfsec in PRs can be noisy; we will run a focused ruleset first and expand.
- Full Terratest coverage is costly; prioritize networking/security modules first (VPC, routing, IAM, KMS).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: self-service UI in Console (tracked separately), private backend appliance-specific state handling (follow-up).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Isabel Moreno: Created ticket after SRE/Privacy sync. Initial proposal attached in Confluence (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Private+IaC+CI-CD+Proposal).

2025-02-20 - Arjun Patel: Spike completed on GitHub Actions runner config and remote state; confirmed S3+DynamoDB pattern works for our cross-account setup. See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2341

2025-02-24 - Security (Lina Chen): Reviewed policy list. Mandatory: no public S3, restrict security group egress rules, KMS key rotation enforced. Suggested adding Conftest rule for IAM wide permissions.

2025-02-26 - Arjun Patel: Implemented baseline pipeline in infra repo. Stages: lint -> plan (artifacts) -> opa-check -> wait-for-approval -> apply. Pipeline YAML snippet: 

name: terraform-pr
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  lint-plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: terraform fmt
        run: terraform fmt -check
      - name: tflint
        run: tflint --config .tflint.hcl
      - name: terraform init
        run: terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
      - name: terraform plan
        run: terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -out=plan.out
      - name: opa/conftest
        run: conftest test -p policies/ plan.out

(Full pipeline at https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/.github/workflows/terraform-pr.yml).
